haiku-low.q1: A message arriving on the domain-events topic starts work. The core app publishes business events there, and the unchanged outbox relay may publish duplicates. The dispatcher reads the topic.
haiku-low.q2: The dispatcher matches active subscriptions by account_id and event type or '*', inserting one pending row per match. A unique key on (event_id, subscription_id) makes a repeated message insert nothing.
haiku-low.q3: It covers the exact stored event JSON text, prefixed by current unix seconds t as '<t>.<body>'. It is computed on every attempt, because t must be current.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx marks delivered. 410 dead-letters the row and disables the subscription. Other 4xx (except 408, 429) dead-letter with no retry. 408, 429, 5xx, timeouts and connection errors retry up to 8 attempts, then dead-letter.
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails, per the retry schedule.
haiku-low.q6: In the service's own Postgres deliveries table: status, attempts, next-attempt time, lease, and last status code or error are stored on the row.
haiku-low.q7: It waits as a pending row in the deliveries table with a next-attempt time. Workers poll about once per second and claim due rows, so the queue is not used for delay.
haiku-low.q8: The 60 s lease expires and another worker claims the row. The crashed attempt still counts toward the 8 attempts, and the receiver may get the same delivery id twice.
haiku-low.q9: Dead rows stay in the service's deliveries table with reason and last status or error. Replay keeps the id, sets status to pending, resets attempts to 0, and makes it due now.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header carrying the delivery id lets receivers dedupe. The id is the same on every attempt and after replay, so it does not change.
haiku-low.q11: Those pending rows are marked dead with reason 'subscription disabled' at their next claim, and are not sent.
haiku-low.q12: Yes. The rules state there is no ordering between events, and delivery is at-least-once.

sonnet.q1: A message arriving on the `domain-events` topic; the core app (via the outbox relay) publishes it, and the dispatcher reads it.
sonnet.q2: The dispatcher selects active subscriptions with the event's account_id whose event_types contain the event type or '*', and inserts one pending delivery row for each. A unique key on (event_id, subscription_id) makes a repeated message insert nothing.
sonnet.q3: HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<body>` (t = current unix seconds, body = exact event JSON text), using the subscription's secret. It is computed again on every attempt, because receivers reject a t older than 5 minutes.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: delivered. 410: dead letter with reason gone, subscription disabled (status disabled, reason gone), and its other pending rows dead-lettered. Other 4xx except 408/429: dead letter at once, no retry. 408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error: retry if fewer than 8 attempts used, otherwise dead letter.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts (a replay resets attempts to 0 and gives a fresh cycle of 8). The wait before attempt 3 is 2 minutes.
sonnet.q6: In the deliveries table of the service's own Postgres database: status (pending/delivered/dead), attempts, next-attempt time, lease, and the last status code or error (plus dead_at and reason for dead rows).
sonnet.q7: It waits in the deliveries table as a pending row with its next-attempt time set and the lease cleared. Workers poll about once per second and claim due pending rows, which triggers the attempt.
sonnet.q8: The lease (60 s) expires and another worker claims the row again and resends. The crashed attempt still counts toward the 8, and the receiver may see the same delivery id twice and dedupes.
sonnet.q9: In the same deliveries table, with status dead, a dead_at time, reason and last status or error, kept 14 days. A replay keeps the delivery id, sets status back to pending, resets attempts to 0, and makes it due now. Replay is refused if the subscription is disabled.
sonnet.q10: The delivery id, sent as the X-Webhook-Id header. It does not change between retries or after a replay.
sonnet.q11: They become dead at their next claim, with reason `subscription disabled`, without being sent. (On a 410, the other pending rows are also dead-lettered immediately.)
sonnet.q12: Yes. There is no ordering between events.
